context.goal: An ERP agent can inspect an explicitly identified Task and obtain sufficient authoritative current stage context through the configured public task-management interface without acquiring ownership, reading an unrelated global overview or guessing query semantics.

definition_of_done: A focused integration scenario obtains the exact Task and sufficient current context without an ownership mutation or broad overview and independently checks required contract fields against the provider result.

Documented examples have independently checked literal argv, mandatory arguments and operation-appropriate links for the selected provider interface; provider query semantics and the shared harness view implementation are reused.
draft.goal: An ERP agent can inspect an explicitly identified Task and obtain sufficient authoritative current stage context through the configured public task-management interface without acquiring ownership, reading an unrelated global overview or guessing query semantics.
requirements: The existing ERP proxy command is extended only to forward the authorized public Poise Task-code/current-context operation and adapt its response. Poise implements the read-only lookup semantics; ERP does not implement its own lookup and does not use bootstrap as a read workaround.
Task code, correlation query ID and caller identity remain distinct; missing or ambiguous selection produces explicit diagnostics rather than ID rewriting or silent fallback to a global list.

The selected context preserves current Task identity/version, stage, scope, criteria, template, evidence obligations and continuation supplied by the authoritative owner; a summary card is not represented as the complete stage contract.

ERP instructions, examples and semantic reference links provide the exact configured read-only invocation and distinguish it from intentional ownership acquisition and genuine work discovery; no direct lifecycle-database query substitutes for the public API.

The same proxy-only boundary applies to every ERP workflow for Tasks, requirements and lifecycle operations: use the public Poise tools, preserve native identity and ownership, and introduce no local domain engine, direct lifecycle-database SQL, second storage or duplicate implementation. Portable provider work is consumed through its declared public integration surface.
